title: Retry dry runs must stay annotation-free; ::notice only after a real rerun request
answers: retry workflow dry run prints a rerun annotation by mistake
why does the retry dry run show no notice
where is the rerun notice emitted in retry.sh
rerun annotation missing or emitted before gh run rerun
body:
Symptom: A dry run of the retry workflow shows a "Rerun failed jobs" annotation, or a rerun annotation appears for a run that was never rerun.
Root cause: .github/workflows/retry.sh:rerun prints either a plain "Would rerun failed jobs for <workflow>" line (dry run, early return) or the ::notice line after `gh run rerun`.
Fix pattern: Keep the `dry_run` early return before any gh call and emit `::notice title=Rerun failed jobs::<workflow>: <run url>` only after `gh run rerun` has been invoked. Dry-run output stays a plain echo that includes the workflow filename.
Constraints: Do not move the ::notice above the gh call or into the dry-run branch. The notice text is the reviewer-visible record of a rerun request, so it must name the workflow filename and the run URL.
applies: Applies to the rerun() function in .github/workflows/retry.sh and any new output it prints; does not cover retry.yml's job logic.
says: Dry runs of the retry workflow mistakenly display rerun annotations on pull requests.
Reviewers see rerun notices even when the pipeline was never actually restarted.
A rerun notification appeared on the check run before any retry happened.
Keep dry run retry checks silent so notices appear only after actual reruns.
Simulation runs should output plain logs instead of creating reviewer-visible rerun notices.
search: The rerun() function in .github/workflows/retry.sh must keep dry-run output annotation-free, emitting ::notice only after gh run rerun executes an actual retry. Dry runs must exit early before any gh invocation, outputting a plain echo containing the workflow filename. Applies to rerun() in retry.sh and excludes retry.yml; ::notice must not precede the gh call or enter the dry-run branch, and must record the workflow filename and run URL.
